---
title: "Airport surface events"
description: "How OPDI finds when an aircraft enters and leaves the taxiways, aprons, stands, runway thresholds, hangars and de-icing pads of an airport. Not validated."
---

## What it is

An airport is made of areas with different uses. OPDI publishes an event each
time an aircraft enters or leaves one of them:

| Area | Meaning | Event types |
|---|---|---|
| Taxiway | A path on which aircraft move between the runways and the parking areas. | `entry-taxiway`, `exit-taxiway` |
| Apron | An area where aircraft park, board passengers, load and refuel. | `entry-apron`, `exit-apron` |
| Stand (`parking_position`) | One marked parking position for one aircraft, usually on an apron. | `entry-parking_position`, `exit-parking_position` |
| Runway threshold | The start of the part of the runway that may be used for landing, marked by white stripes. | `entry-threshold`, `exit-threshold` |
| Hangar | A building in which aircraft are kept or maintained. | `entry-hangar`, `exit-hangar` |
| De-icing pad | An area where ice and snow are removed from aircraft before take-off. | `entry-deicing_pad`, `exit-deicing_pad` |

The runway itself is not in this list. Its use is described by the runway
events: see [Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd) and
[Runway milestones](runway-milestones.qmd).

Each event carries the position, altitude, distance flown and time passed of
the state vector it was taken from. Its `info` field holds the OpenStreetMap
identifier of the area (`osm_id`), its kind (`osm_aeroway`), its name or
number in OpenStreetMap if it has one (`osm_ref`, for example the stand
number), the airport (`osm_airport`), the time spent in the area
(`opdi_time_in_use_s`, seconds), the aircraft address (`osn_icao24`) and the
call sign (`osn_flight_id`). The events carry the version `events_v0.3.0`.

The stand events are also used to find the block times and the stand columns
of the flight list (see [Block times](block-times.qmd)).

## How it is computed

1. **Airport layouts.** The areas come from OpenStreetMap, the open map of the
   world, for every large and medium airport. An area mapped as a line (for
   example a taxiway centre line) or a point (for example a stand) is widened
   into a surface, using the width given in OpenStreetMap or a default width
   for its kind. Each area is then covered with small hexagonal cells (H3 cells
   of resolution 12, each about 300 m²).
2. **Samples near the ground.** The method uses the cleaned state vectors of
   each track (see [Trajectory cleaning](trajectory-cleaning.qmd)) that have a
   position and that are either marked as on the ground by the aircraft, or at
   most 2,000 ft above the airport. The height above the airport is the
   barometric altitude minus the airport's elevation; for this test the lower
   of the departure and destination airports' heights is used.
3. **Match.** A state vector is in an area when its H3 cell is one of the
   area's cells and the area belongs to an airport that the flight list names
   for the flight: the departure airport, the destination airport or one of
   the other close airports listed (see
   [Departure and destination airports](airports.qmd)).
4. **Visits.** The matched state vectors of one track in one area, in time
   order, form a visit. A silence of more than 300 s starts a new visit.
5. **Events.** The first state vector of a visit gives the `entry-` event and
   the last one gives the `exit-` event, each with the position, altitude and
   measurements of that state vector.
6. A visit made of a single state vector, or whose entry and exit fall in the
   same second, has no duration and is dropped.

The [plausibility checks](plausibility-checks.qmd) then leave out an entry or
exit made while the aircraft was flying: more than 1,500 ft above the airport,
faster than 80 kt, and with no state vector within 60 s flagged on the
ground.

## Reference data

None. The airport operator records used for the runway and block times (see
[Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd#reference-data)) name the stand of
each movement, but give no time of entry into or exit from any area of the
airport. No other source of these times was available.

## Validation method

Not validated. Validation would need the times at which aircraft enter and
leave areas of the airport, as recorded for example by a surface movement
radar or by the airport's own systems.

Two parts of the data could be checked against the airport operator records
without new data, but have not been: the stand of `exit-parking_position` at
the departure airport against the departure stand in the records, and the
stand of `entry-parking_position` at the destination against the arrival
stand. The stand events are used indirectly in the block times, which were
validated (see [Block times](block-times.qmd#results)).

## Limitations

- None of these events has been compared with reference data.
- The events need the aircraft to be received on the ground. Away from the
  best-covered airports, ground reception is often missing and so are the
  events.
- The events depend on OpenStreetMap. An area that is not mapped, or mapped in
  the wrong place, gives no event or a wrong one. Names in `osm_ref` follow
  OpenStreetMap and can differ from the names the airport uses.
- Only large and medium airports are covered, and only those that the flight
  list names for the flight.
- The H3 cells are about 20 m across, and the state vectors are 5 s apart.
  Entry and exit times can therefore be off by up to one sampling interval,
  and a small area (such as a runway threshold) crossed between two state
  vectors is missed.
- A visit made of a single state vector is dropped, so short passages over
  small areas are under-counted.
- Areas overlap: a stand usually lies on an apron, and a taxiway can cross an
  apron. One movement can therefore produce several entry and exit events at
  the same time. Where the aircraft enters (or leaves) two areas of the same
  kind (for example two stands drawn over each other) at the same report, one
  event is given, and it names the area with the smallest `osm_id`, so every
  run names the same area.
- An aircraft taxiing past stands enters and leaves the stand areas it passes
  over. An `entry-parking_position` event does not mean that the aircraft
  parked there.
- State vectors up to 2,000 ft above the airport are matched to the areas. The
  plausibility checks remove an event only when the aircraft was more than
  1,500 ft above the airport, faster than 80 kt and not reported on the
  ground, so an aircraft passing low or slowly over an area can still produce
  an entry and an exit.
- De-icing pads are mapped in OpenStreetMap at few airports, and are used
  mainly in winter.
